title: The Flying Machine That Lost to Two Bike Mechanics

shots.line: December eighth, nineteen-oh-three.
shots.scene: Date card DEC 8, 1903 over a freezing dusk river

shots.line: A freezing river in Washington, D.C.
shots.scene: Wide: icy Potomac at dusk, ice floes, Capitol dome far away

shots.line: A giant flying machine sits on a catapult, on top of a houseboat.
shots.scene: Houseboat with Langley's giant tandem-wing Aerodrome on the catapult, crowd on the bank

shots.line: Its creator is Samuel Langley, head of the Smithsonian.
shots.scene: Langley (trench + fedora) on the riverbank, arms crossed, name label

shots.line: The U.S. Army has given him fifty thousand dollars.
shots.scene: Card: U.S. ARMY grant counter to $50,000

shots.line: The whole country expects him to build the first airplane.
shots.scene: Crowd on the bank cheers, newspaper spins in 'WILL MAN FLY?'

shots.line: The catapult fires.
shots.scene: Insert: catapult fires, speed lines

shots.line: The machine snaps apart and plunges straight into the Potomac.
shots.scene: Aerodrome snaps apart and plunges into the river, splash

shots.line: Its pilot is dragged from the icy water, lucky to be alive.
shots.scene: bigFace pilot (Manly) gasping, water drops

shots.line: It was Langley's second crash in two months.
shots.scene: Card: two crashes OCT 7 and DEC 8, X marks

shots.line: After the first one, the New York Times predicted a real flying machine might
shots.scene: Newspaper editorial spins in: 'flying machines which do not fly'

shots.line: take one to ten million years.
shots.scene: Counter spins to 10,000,000 YEARS

shots.line: It took nine days.
shots.scene: Calendar flips 8 -> 17: 9 DAYS

shots.line: On December seventeenth, at Kitty Hawk, two bicycle mechanics
shots.scene: Kitty Hawk dunes establishing, windy, Flyer on its rail

shots.line: from Dayton, Ohio, flew for twelve seconds.
shots.scene: Wright Flyer lifts off, Wilbur runs alongside, 12 SEC timer

shots.line: Orville and Wilbur Wright.
shots.scene: Two-shot: Orville and Wilbur on the dunes, names

shots.line: No government money. By most accounts, they spent less than a thousand dollars.
shots.scene: Compare bars: LANGLEY $50,000 vs WRIGHTS < $1,000

shots.line: But the story didn't end there.
shots.scene: BUT... line

shots.line: Years later, the Smithsonian modified Langley's machine,
shots.scene: 1914: rebuilt Aerodrome hops off a lake on pontoons

shots.line: flew it, and claimed it could have flown first.
shots.scene: Museum hall: Langley's machine on display, glowing sign 'FIRST?'

shots.line: The Wrights were furious.
shots.scene: bigFace Orville furious

shots.line: Orville sent their original airplane to a museum in London.
shots.scene: Map: crate ships the Flyer across the ocean to LONDON

shots.line: It didn't come home to America until nineteen forty-eight.
shots.scene: Years spin to 1948, the Flyer comes home to the museum

shots.line: Would you have bet on the bike mechanics?
shots.scene: Split: Langley vs the Wright brothers, '?'

shots.line: Follow for more.
shots.scene: End card FOLLOW FOR MORE
